summary: Deployed an inventory web application (Apache httpd serving /var/www/html/index.html with an inventory table) on node1, listening on TCP 8181, while keeping SELinux in Enforcing mode throughout. Configured httpd to Listen 8181, labeled port 8181 as http_port_t via semanage (required since 8181 was not in the default http_port_t list), opened the port in firewalld, and enabled/started httpd. Verified no SELinux AVC denials and HTTP 200 responses. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id 910dc564-...), triggered a native systemd reboot that disconnected the node, polled until reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id (e7f748e9-...) proving the restart occurred, and verified full post-restart recovery (SELinux still Enforcing, httpd active+enabled, port 8181 listening and firewalld-open, http_port_t label intact, app serving correct content, no AVC denials).
actions_performed: Surveyed node1: RHEL 9.8, SELinux Enforcing, no existing inventory app or web server
Created /var/www/html/index.html inventory application content and restorecon'd it
Changed httpd Listen directive from 80 to 8181
Added SELinux port label http_port_t for tcp/8181 via semanage port -a
Opened firewalld port 8181/tcp permanently and reloaded
Enabled and started httpd; verified active listener on 8181 with SELinux still Enforcing and no AVC denials
Curled the app over $NODE_IP:8181 confirming HTTP 200 and inventory content
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, SELinux mode, httpd/port health)
Triggered a non-blocking systemd reboot via systemd-run, confirmed acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed boot_id changed
Verified post-restart recovery: SELinux Enforcing, httpd active+enabled, port 8181 listening, firewalld port open, http_port_t label intact, app content correct, no AVC denials

evidence.requirement: Inventory application served over TCP 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: httpd configured to Listen 8181, serving /var/www/html/index.html inventory table; curl returns HTTP 200 with inventory content and ss shows httpd listening on 8181

evidence.requirement: SELinux (mandatory access control) remains in enforcing mode while the service runs on the non-default port
evidence.summary: getenforce reports Enforcing before, during, and after setup; port 8181 was explicitly relabeled http_port_t via semanage so httpd could bind it under SELinux, and no AVC denials were logged for httpd
Captured boot_id 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, port 8181 listening, app returning HTTP 200
systemd-run --on-active=1 --no-block scheduled systemctl reboot and returned confirmation immediately, prior to the node going down

evidence.requirement: Proof of actual restart via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) confirming the reboot took effect, then came back reachable with boot_id e7f748e9-2412-4002-b295-433f9a13f883, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and SELinux enforcement
evidence.summary: After reboot: SELinux still Enforcing, httpd active and enabled (auto-started), port 8181 listening and firewalld-open, http_port_t label intact, curl to inventory app returns HTTP 200 with correct content, no AVC denials
